subject: Setup a sampler's object for each chain ?

messages.author: d128bd7b4bae8e43
messages.subject: Setup a sampler's object for each chain ?
parts:
Hi all,

In a custom sampler I use a matrix generated by some function of mine. This matrix depend on the current values of the model.
Currently I recalculate the matrix at each iteration, which is terribly inefficient (the calculation implies several loops and lots of condition checking...), while I could save the matrix and update only the values that should be updated at some point in the sampler.

My problem is for the initialization of this matrix. Since it depends on the model values, if I just create it in the setup part, it will be initialized with the values used for the model creation and any chain using a different starting point will most likely generate errors.

Is there any way to re-setup a sampler at the beggining of a chain ?
The only thing I can think of otherwise would be to initialize it with only zeros, and check its condition when I need it, and compute it completely if it's full-zeros, which is not a very sexy solution...

Thank you,

Rémi

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Setup a sampler's object for each chain ?
parts:
Rémi, perhaps someone on the list will have a better solution for you.  My suggestion here is basically what you suggested - setting a flag (0/1 binary variable) in the setup code to indicate whether the matrix is "initialized".  The flag starts at 0, and the matrix initially is all zeros (or anything else).  Then, when you first use the matrix in the run function, check this flag.  If it's 0, then initialize the matrix (and set the flag to 1).  Also, in the reset method of the sampler, set this flag back to 0, so that on future MCMC chains (perhaps with different initial values in the model), the matrix will be initialized again, using the current values in the model.

A quick code sketch is below.  Hopefully this helps, even if it's not elegant, or maybe someone else will have a better suggestion.

Cheers,
Daniel


my_sampler <- nimbleFunction(
    contains = sampler_BASE,
    setup = function(...) {
        ...
        matrixInitializedFlag <- 0
        matrix <- array(0, c(N, M))
    }
    run = function() {
        ## when the matrix is first used:
        if(matrixInitializedFlag == 0) {
            matrixInitializedFlag <<- 1     ## use double assignment operator <<-
            ## initialize matrix here       ## also use <<- here to assign values into the matrix
            ...
        }
        ...
    }
    methods = list(
        reset = funtion() {
            ...
            matrixInitializedFlag <<- 0     ## use <<- here
        }
    )
)

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Setup a sampler's object for each chain ?
parts:
The reset method is called at the beginning of every MCMC chain, unless you initiate the chain using the mcmc's internal run method and also providing the reset = FALSE argument (which is uncommon):

mcmc$run(10000, reset = FALSE)

Setting the matrix inside the reset method sounds like a very good idea, Rémi.
